groups.name: Characters widely known by a name that is not their legal birth name
groups.explanation: Don Draper's real name is Dick Whitman, an identity he stole from a dead soldier; Jimmy McGill later adopts the alias Saul Goodman and operates under it for years; Offred is a patronymic imposed by the Gilead regime — her real name is June Osborne; Nucky Thompson's given name is Enoch Lewis Thompson — 'Nucky' is a lifelong nickname that masks his formal identity, and in Boardwalk Empire his constructed public persona is central to his character. Each is known to audiences by a name that obscures or replaces their birth identity.

groups.name: TV characters played by actors born outside the United States who play American characters
groups.explanation: Gregory House is an American doctor played by Hugh Laurie, who is British; Cersei Lannister is played by Lena Headey, who is British — however Cersei is not American, she is fictional/Westerosi. This group concept needs a consistent framing. Revised: actors born outside the US playing characters who are coded as belonging to a specific non-American nationality or fictional world: Hugh Laurie (British) plays House (American-coded) — does not fit a non-American character framing. Cleanest framing: non-American actors playing roles in American prestige television: Hugh Laurie (British) as House M.D.; Lena Headey (British) as Cersei Lannister in Game of Thrones (HBO); Tatiana Maslany (Canadian) as Rachel Duncan in Orphan Black (BBC America); Wentworth Miller (British-born) as Michael Scofield in Prison Break (Fox). All four are non-American actors who became iconic in major American television productions.

groups.name: TV shows renewed for a second season before their first season finished airing
groups.explanation: Fleabag was recommissioned by BBC Three for a second series before its first series finished airing; The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel was renewed by Amazon for Season 2 before Season 1 had completed its release; Fawlty Towers was commissioned by the BBC for a second series before the first series had finished its transmission run in 1975; Riverdale, the show featuring Betty Cooper, was renewed by The CW before Season 1 had aired its finale. All four received early renewal before their debut seasons concluded.

groups.name: The first name in the tile text is also the name of a living thing found in a garden
groups.explanation: Phoebe (Waller-Bridge) — the Eastern Phoebe is a flycatcher bird that nests in gardens and eaves; Rust (Cohle) — rust is a common fungal disease that attacks garden plants such as roses and beans; Basil (Fawlty) — basil is a culinary herb cultivated in gardens worldwide; Midge (Maisel) — a midge is a tiny flying insect ubiquitous around garden plants and water. Each tile's opening first name is also independently the name of something biological encountered in a garden: a bird, a plant pathogen, an herb, and an insect.
